claim: DeepEye-SQL's Semantic Value Retrieval module extracts unique values from TEXT columns and embeds them so the LLM is supplied a relevant subset of real database values, preventing hallucinated or mismatched filter values (the grounding problem).
quote: DeepEye-SQL incorporates a Semantic Value Retrieval module that proactively supplies the LLM with a contextually relevant subset of database values. Instead of indexing every value, selective extraction is performed targeting columns of type TEXT as they are the primary source of ambiguity and value-related hallucinations.

claim: Vanna.AI (23,582 GitHub stars) is a RAG text-to-SQL framework that embeds DDL statements, business documentation, and example SQL queries into a vector store and retrieves the most relevant pieces by similarity to build the LLM prompt.
quote: Vanna works in two easy steps - train a RAG model on your data, and then ask questions... Whenever you ask a new question, Vanna will retrieve 10 most relevant pieces of training data and use it as part of the prompt to generate the SQL.

claim: Vanna stores embeddings of DDL, documentation, and SQL examples in a vector store and at query time retrieves the 10 most relevant pieces of training data via semantic matching to inject into the SQL-generation prompt.
quote: Whenever you ask a new question, Vanna will retrieve 10 most relevant pieces of training data and use it as part of the LLM prompt to generate the SQL.

claim: DAIL-SQL (635 GitHub stars) selects few-shot examples by joint question- and query-level similarity, masking domain-specific tokens then filtering candidates by query (SQL) similarity, achieving 86.6% execution accuracy on the Spider leaderboard with GPT-4.
quote: DAIL-SQL refreshes the Spider leaderboard with 86.6% execution accuracy and wins the first place... DAIL Selection retrieves examples by jointly considering question- and query-level similarity.

claim: LlamaIndex's PGVectorSQLQueryEngine teaches the LLM to emit SQL using pgvector's <-> nearest-neighbor operator with a [query_vector] placeholder, unifying semantic row retrieval (ORDER BY embedding <-> query) and structured WHERE filtering in a single SQL statement.
quote: We use specialized pgvector syntax (`<->`) to do nearest neighbors/semantic search to a given vector from an embeddings column... This allows you to do both semantic search and structured querying, _all_ within SQL.

claim: For large schemas, schema linking combines a retrieval module and column selector: top-k columns per query keyword are retrieved by embedding-based semantic similarity between keywords and column descriptions, so only relevant columns are passed to the SQL-generating LLM.
quote: Based on semantic similarity between keywords and column descriptions, the top-k columns for each keyword can be retrieved.
